HomeStyle Retailers - Q2 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeStyle Retailers Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please press star one to ask a question. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeStyle Retailers' results for the Q2 FY2024. Joining me on today’s call are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Merchandising Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Stores Officer; David Ruiz, Chief Marketing Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Jamie Thompson.

Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeStyle Retailers' performance for the Q2 FY2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Let me start by sharing our overall company performance highlights. We had a standout quarter, exceeding our guidance across the board and underscoring the resilience of our brick-and-mortar model amid a choppy retail macro. Total net sales reached $2.52 billion, up 5.2% year-over-year and beating our $2.45 billion guide by 2.9%. This marks our sixth straight quarter of positive comps, with company-wide same-store sales climbing 3.8%—our strongest Q2 comp since 2019, outpacing the retail sector average of flat to down 1% as reported by the NRF.

Driving this top-line momentum was robust traffic growth of 2.1%, fueled by our Value Refresh pricing initiative, which resonated strongly with middle-market consumers facing persistent inflation pressures. Average ticket rose 1.6% to $128, reflecting higher AURs in big-ticket categories like kitchen appliances and outdoor living—up 4.2%—as customers traded up within our private-label HomeForge line, which now accounts for 28% of sales, a 300-basis-point YoY increase. Units per transaction held steady at 2.4, but we saw meaningful UPT lift in softlines like bedding and decor, up 5%, thanks to targeted merchandising resets in our 1,250 core stores.

Gross margin expanded 120 basis points to 38.5%, our highest Q2 level in five years, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward higher-margin owned brands and improved freight costs following the unwind of Red Sea disruptions. We also clawed back 50 basis points from shrink mitigation, including our nationwide rollout of AI-powered inventory sensors in 40% of stores—reducing out-of-stocks by 15% and ORC losses by 22%. SG&A as a percentage of sales deleveraged 80 basis points to 28.2%, reflecting disciplined labor scheduling via our proprietary Workforce Optimizer tool and lower occupancy costs from lease optimizations.

Adjusted operating income hit $412 million, up 14.7% YoY, while EBITDA soared 18% to $458 million—a 19.2% margin, well ahead of our long-term 18% target. Diluted EPS came in at $1.42, smashing consensus by $0.18. Free cash flow generation was equally impressive at $320 million, enabling $150 million in share repurchases and a 12% dividend hike announced today—our 17th consecutive increase.

Regionally, performance was bifurcated but broadly positive. The Sunbelt markets—Florida, Texas, and the Carolinas—led with 6.2% comps, powered by population in-migration and our aggressive new-store pipeline of 25 openings YTD, including three next-gen Hub & Flow prototypes averaging 45,000 sq ft with dedicated curbside zones and micro-fulfillment centers. These pilots are delivering 12% higher SSS than legacy formats. The Midwest and West Coast posted solid 4.1% comps, bolstered by strong patio and grill sell-through amid an early summer season. Northeast lagged at 1.2%, pressured by unseasonable weather and softer urban traffic, but we're countering with pop-up experiential zones partnering with local influencers, mirroring successful plays by peers like Williams-Sonoma.

Strategically, our omnichannel integration continues to supercharge brick-and-mortar. BOPIS now represents 22% of digital orders—up from 18% last year—with store-fulfilled e-comm sales contributing 3.2 points to overall comps. We've invested $75 million YTD in supply chain resilience, including a new 1.2 million sq ft DC in Georgia optimized for same-day regional delivery, reducing lead times by 30% and positioning us against pure-plays like Wayfair. Loyalty membership grew 11% to 18 million active households, with enrollees spending 2.5x more and transacting 40% more frequently—key to defending share in a value-conscious environment where discounters like TJX and Walmart are gaining AUR traction.

Macro tailwinds include stabilizing consumer sentiment and housing turnover up 8% YoY per NAR data, which bodes well for our $15 billion home improvement TAM. Challenges persist—labor availability in key markets and potential tariff headwinds on imported hardlines—but our 4.2x inventory turns (up from 3.9x) and $1.1 billion cash position give us ample dry powder.

Turning now to digital marketing effectiveness, as we navigate a challenging retail macro marked by persistent inflation at around 3.2% CPI, softening consumer confidence per the Conference Board index, and intensifying competition from pure-play e-commerce giants like Amazon—our brick-and-mortar footprint remains our competitive moat. With over 1,200 stores across North America and Europe, generating 68% of our quarterly revenue from physical channels, driving store traffic through digital levers is paramount. We've delivered outsized returns that directly fueled a 12% YoY increase in comparable store sales and a 22% lift in foot traffic.

In Q2, our total digital ad spend reached $162 million, up 18% YoY but flat sequentially as we optimized for efficiency amid softer demand for big-ticket home goods like appliances and furniture. Overall ROAS hit 8.2x, surpassing our internal target of 7x and up from 6.4x a year ago. Performance search on Google Ads and Bing delivered 12.1x ROAS, driven by high-intent queries around energy-efficient refrigerators amid rising utility costs. Social media, primarily Meta and TikTok, clocked in at 7.8x, while emerging CTV campaigns on Roku and Hulu achieved 9.5x, thanks to upper-funnel awareness for our private-label Essentials Home line.

Customer acquisition cost improved to $28 per new store visitor, down 14% YoY, with AOV at $142 in stores attributed to digital campaigns, 21% above our all-store average. Conversion rates from digital touchpoints to in-store purchases stood at 4.7%, validated through our proprietary multi-touch attribution model using first-party data from our loyalty app, now with 28 million active users—a 15% YoY increase.

These gains result from targeted initiatives like doubling down on AI-powered personalization via Google Cloud's Vertex AI, powering dynamic creative optimization in Meta Advantage+ shopping campaigns with hyper-personalized carousels based on in-app behavior, yielding a 32% uplift in click-through rates and 25% higher store attribution via geofencing pixels.

Post-iOS 14.5 and cookieless shift, we've accelerated first-party data strategy with our Customer Data Platform on Adobe Experience Platform, aggregating 85% of signals from owned channels like email, SMS, app, and in-store Wi-Fi. This fueled a 40% ROAS boost in prospecting. We're piloting Google's Privacy Sandbox Topics API, yielding ROAS parity to third-party segments.

On incrementality, geo-holdout tests showed digital drove an 18% lift in incremental store visits during Labor Day promotion, measured via Verkada and Placer.ai. Marketing mix modeling with Nielsen confirms $2.10 in total omnichannel revenue per $1 spent, 62% to brick-and-mortar.

Regionally, US ROAS hit 9.1x, propelled by suburban TikTok Shops BOPIS jumps of 28% YoY. Europe at 6.2x up 22% YoY with localized campaigns for UK/Germany influencers on sustainable EcoEssentials bamboo furniture. Asia-Pacific pilots at 7.5x via WeChat.

Strategically, our retail media network HomeStyle Connect generated $12 million in Q3 revenue at 15x ROAS for partners, 70% flowing back to performance. Ahead, $50 million in FY25 for causal AI from Shaped.ai and headless CMS for AR previews. Digital contributed $1.3 billion in attributable revenue, 31% of total, raising FY24 ROAS guide to 8.0x-8.5x for 5-7% comp growth.

Regarding the number of store openings and closings, we've been laser-focused on right-sizing our footprint amid softening mall traffic, inflationary leases, and omnichannel shifts. In Q2, we opened 18 net new stores, with 25 gross openings and 7 closures. This added 425,000 sq ft gross, offset by 85,000 sq ft closed, for net 340,000 sq ft or 1.2% growth. YTD, 32 net new (42 opens, 10 closes), on track for 65-75 net full-year.

Openings: 14 core big-box (18,000 sq ft avg) in Sunbelt—7 Florida (Orlando/Tampa), 4 Texas (DFW/Houston), 3 Atlanta. 11 express (8-12k sq ft) urban infill Nashville/Charlotte with BOPIS lockers. New stores deliver 15% above avg sales/sq ft.

Closures: 7 legacy mall anchors (12k sq ft avg), 0.8% of 850-store portfolio, 30% below $450 system avg sales/sq ft, -10% comps trailing 24 mo, due to Class B/C malls, remote work.

Trailing 12-mo churn 2.1% (down from 3.5%), via Project Optimize AI site analytics with Esri/Buxton, improving first-year ROI 22%.

Sunbelt 65% openings, Florida new comps +18% with coffee bars/AR mirrors. Northeast/Midwest no opens, 4 closes (Buffalo/Detroit). West flat with Phoenix remodel.

We prioritize productivity: sales/sq ft up 4.2% YoY to $462. Closures save $45M rent, to 150 remodels with RFID/shop-ins. H2 favors express (60%), AI pruning if rents >12% sales.

On regional performance variations, company-wide SSS grew 2.1% in Q2, beating flat-+1% guide, with 1.8% traffic, 0.3% AUR to $42.50, UPT +0.2% to 2.4. Gross margins +110bps to 38.2%, turns 5.2x, shrink 1.6%.

Northeast (25%, 310 doors): +4.6% comps, traffic +3.5%, kitchen/bath +12%, UPT 2.7, margins 39.5% +180bps via NJ DC, Store 2.0 AR kiosks +22% conversion. Heat offset HVAC promo. H2 +5%.

Southeast (30%, 365 doors): flat 0.1%, traffic -0.8%, hurricanes -150bps (12 stores/4 days), apparel -3%. Margins 37.8% +50bps, markdowns -18%, Atlanta DC 96% in-stocks. Value private label +15%, 8 rural closes. Q3 +1.5%.

Midwest (22%, 265 doors): +3.2%, traffic +2.1%, AUR +0.8% tools/lawn, margins 38.9% +140bps RFID shrink -12%. BOPIS 28%, $25M agronomy bays. H2 +3.5-4%.

West (23%, 280 doors): -1.4%, wildfires/Amazon -8% traffic, AUR -0.5%, margins 37.4% -20bps promo, inventory -7% turns 5.5x. Starline video +18% conv, 15 relos, Uber Eats pilot. Q3 +0.5%.

Dispersions 600bps, 20/20/20 playbook (20% capex remodels/digital, 20 stores closed/relocated, 20% private label). Q3 SSS +1.5-2.5%, Northeast/Midwest lead, $180M capex DCs/RFID.

Next, on marketing and advertising expense trends, total expenses were $152 million in Q2, up 12% YoY from $136 million, at 4.2% of net sales—flat seq, +20bps YoY. This supports traffic/conversion in 1,200+ stores amid 2.1% SSS, 3% deflation big-ticket.

Traditional media 28% ($43M, -15% YoY), cut print 25%, pivot to HomeStyle Media $28M third-party (+45% YoY), offsets 18% ad costs.

Digital 62% ($94M, up from 48%), Google/YouTube $41M +22% ROAS 5.8x hyper-local SEM. Meta $32M +18%, CPA $28 -11% AI DCO 1,200 variants. Social/influencer $12M +35%, 250 micro DIY +24% traffic shoppable Reels. Programmatic/CTV $9M 3.2x Trade Desk Sunbelt.

First-party CDP Tealium + Rewards 45M members +8% YoY, 35% personalized, geo push 15% BOPIS. Criteo clean rooms +22% attribution.

Southeast spend/store -7% hurricane co-op Sherwin-Williams. Northeast +18% throttled TV +TikTok 4.5x. Canada flat CAD12M +10% ROAS Shopify.

FY spend $620-640M 4.1-4.3% sales, 10-13% growth, 25%+ media scale, CAC <$35. Drove 28% Q2 traffic.

Inventory levels year-over-year ended down 9.2% to $2.41 billion from $2.65 billion. Inventory-to-sales 24.6% from 28.1%, DIO 72 from 84 days, ahead 75 target, better than Macy's 78, Target 76. Turns 5.1x from 4.4x.

Apparel 42% -12.4% $1.01B prune loungewear. Footwear/access 28% -7.8% $675M VMI Nike/Crocs 65%. Home/seasonal 30% +2.1% $725M kitchen/holiday.

Sunbelt 38% stores -11.5% DIO 68, footwear 6.2x. Midwest/Northeast 32% -6.8% DIO 78 unemployment 4.2%, markdowns -220bps.

Canada/Mexico 150 stores flat $185M, Canada home +8%, Mexico SKU -5% inflation 5.5%.

AI Palantir/Manhattan 92% SKUs forecast 88% acc, stockouts -18% overstock -22%. RFID 85% apparel/footwear 95% counts, BOPIS 28%. JIT Levi's/UA/Whirlpool 40% Vietnam/Bangladesh, lead 45 days vs 55-60 NRF. DCs Dallas/Chicago -14% freight 70% cross-dock.

Q4 -7-8% YoY, +50bps GM shrink 1.4%, markdown opt vs TJX/Ross/Temu. Brick tactile 4.5x full-price conv.

Finally, some financial outlook commentary. Wrapping a solid Q2 with 3.2% comps—strongest pre-pandemic—our Q3/full FY2024 outlook reflects resilient middle-market, omnichannel, supply opt amid inflation. Tempered for NPD 1.5% non-essential pullback.

Q3 (Oct 2024): Comps +2.0-3.5%, digital +8-10% BrickLane app BOPIS 85% stores, physical +1-2.5% 50 express pilot 15k sq ft +15% sales/sq ft. GM 38.5-39.5% +100bps AI IBM Watson -25% stockouts -18% overstock ForgeHome, nearshore Mexico freight -12%. SG&A 27.0-27.5% Kronos labor 4% wage, $15M savings 20 urban closes SF/NY. EPS $0.85-0.95 +8-12%, shares 145M $200M buyback $120M YTD $28.50 avg. CapEx $180M 75 remodels beauty bars RFID.

FY2024 (Jan 2025): Sales $8.6-8.8B +2.5-4.0%, comps +3.0% Conference Board 103. GM 38.8-39.3% +150bps home 32% durables. Op margin 5.5-6.0%, adj EPS $3.40-3.60 +$0.10 bottom. FCF $450-500M $250M div/buybacks, leverage 2.2x. Inventory $1.4B flat 5.2x turns vs NRF 4.8x.

Midwest/SE 60% +5% TJX-like. West urban -50bps shoplift 1.2% Hayes, Canada flat loonie, 10 Mexico City NAFTA apparel.

LaneLink loyalty 18M 45% pen 3x spend RFID offers. NCR autonomous kiosks 100 stores -30% trans time. Blockchain EcoForge Gen Z 25% digital.

Risks: 3.5% PCE, port strikes, Amazon Prime. Upside: 200 remodels 2025, Walmart Marketplace, M&A Pier 1-like.

Key assumptions: Q3 comps 2.5-4.0%, EPS $0.85-0.95, FY comps 3-5%. Top-line: +150bps traffic -50bps ticket deflation 5-7% apparel vs Shein/Temu, 60/40 store/digital BOPIS 28%. Sunbelt >5% migration, NE/MW flat-+1% weather $50-100k HH NRF. Inventory 12 wks -18% YoY MaxHome +15%.

GM +75-100bps 38.0-38.3% home/elec 42% private 32% Kohl's-like, shrink 1.6% RFID 70-90% SymphonyAI. Freight -20% Red Sea Mexico/Vietnam China <25%, promo 22% markdown <8% Salesforce.

SG&A flat-+25bps 28.5-28.7%, wage 4% UKG 12.5% payroll, mktg 3.8% retail media $45M Q2 Walmart Connect-like.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more details on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Jamie. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q2 FY2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.52 billion, a 5.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 38.5%, primarily driven by favorable product mix shifts to owned brands, lower freight costs post-Red Sea unwind, and shrink reductions from AI sensors and RFID.

Operating expenses were $710 million, representing 28.2% of revenue, benefiting from optimized labor scheduling and lease adjustments. Net income was $290 million, or $1.42 per share. We generated $320 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently down 9.2% year-over-year at $2.41 billion, with improved turns supporting margin discipline.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Mike Patel, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Lisa Chen to discuss store operations, David Ruiz to discuss marketing initiatives, and Elena Vasquez to talk about technology advancements.

Mike Patel, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. This quarter, we launched our expanded HomeForge private-label line in kitchen essentials and outdoor living, which has seen strong uptake with 15% comp growth and now 28% of sales. We are excited about the potential of this new assortment and other upcoming launches in sustainable bedding.

Lisa Chen, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Mike. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented Hub & Flow prototype remodels in select locations with curbside zones and micro-fulfillment, delivering 12% higher SSS and positive early results across our 1,250 doors.

David Ruiz, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. Our Value Refresh campaign has increased brand awareness by 25% and driven 22% foot traffic lift, with ROAS exceeding 8x through targeted digital and retail media efforts.

Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer:
Thank you, David. We have invested in AI-powered inventory sensors and RFID across 40-85% of stores, which has improved out-of-stocks by 15%, cycle count accuracy to 95%, and overall omnichannel fulfillment efficiency.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of persistent inflation on your sales?

Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, Emily. Inflation at 3.2% CPI has pressured middle-market consumers, but our Value Refresh initiative and private-label HomeForge at 28% mix drove 1.6% average ticket growth, with traffic up 2.1% as shoppers sought value in big-ticket categories up 4.2%. We're defending share against discounters via loyalty and omnichannel, keeping comps at 3.8%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert. For Q3, we expect comps in the range of +2.0% to +3.5%, with physical stores at +1% to +2.5% from express pilots and digital accelerating to +8-10% on BOPIS expansion. This assumes traffic gains offset modest ticket pressure from apparel deflation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Bennett with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Bennett (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Laura. We've invested $75 million YTD, including a new 1.2M sq ft Georgia DC cutting lead times 30%, nearshoring to Mexico/Vietnam reducing China to under 25%, JIT with key vendors at 40% receipts, and DC consolidations saving 14% freight. This boosted turns to 4.2x and supported GM expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Hargrove with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Hargrove (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Tom. Our loyalty program grew 11% to 18 million active households, with members spending 2.5x more and transacting 40% more frequently. LaneLink at 45% penetration drives 3x spend via RFID offers, contributing key to comps and defending against value discounters.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Citi. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim (Citi):
Thanks. On inventory, how do you see levels trending into holiday, and any category specifics?

Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer:
Hi Rachel. We're guiding Q4 inventories down another 7-8% YoY, with disciplined 5.1x turns. Apparel down 12.4% post-pruning, home up selectively 2.1% for holiday, supported by 88% AI forecast accuracy and RFID for BOPIS. This positions us for 50bps GM tailwind vs. competitors.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions. I'll now turn the call back over to the team for closing remarks.

Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
